title: Go Maps: Key Facts for Interviews

scenes.line1: How do Go maps really work?
scenes.say: How do Go maps really work? And what catches developers off guard in interviews?

scenes.label: Reference
scenes.sub: Maps are reference types for key-value pairs.
scenes.say: Maps in Go are reference types. They store key-value pairs, and the map itself is a reference, not a copy.
Always initialize a map before use. If you access a missing key, Go returns the zero value for the type, and a boolean shows if the key existed.

scenes.label: Nil
scenes.sub: A nil map can't be written to—only read.
scenes.say: A nil map can't be written to. You can read from it, but any write will panic.

scenes.question: Are Go maps safe for concurrent writes?
scenes.wrong: Yes, Go handles it for you.
scenes.right: No. Concurrent writes cause a runtime panic.
scenes.say: Are Go maps safe for concurrent writes? No—they are not. Concurrent writes will cause a runtime panic.
